overview: This modern Swedish record begins with the atlas’s 1914 snapshot, long after the kingdom itself began. The twentieth century brought broader political participation and changes in housing, family policy and medicine. Surviving appliances, photographs, laws and institutional records make these developments tangible.

periods.title: Voting and social reform
periods.summary: Equal parliamentary voting rights were exercised in the 1921 election.

periods.title: Homes, research and public institutions
periods.summary: Domestic research, medical technology and parental insurance changed opportunities and everyday work.

periods.title: Within the European Union
periods.summary: Sweden joined the European Union in 1995 and continues as a state.

items.text: The 1921 election was the first parliamentary election with equal suffrage for women and men. Five women took seats in 1922. The dates separate winning an election from beginning parliamentary work; neither means representation became equal overnight.

Sweden replaced its two parliamentary chambers with one in 1971. Changing an institution’s structure is different from founding a new country. The elected assembly continued to make laws and supervise government.

All offentlig makt i Sverige utgår från folket means “All public power in Sweden proceeds from the people.” It opens Chapter 1 of the Instrument of Government. This sample follows the official consolidated Swedish text of the law adopted in 1974.

The Home Research Institute was established in 1944 by women’s and homemakers’ organizations, with state funding. Researchers timed tasks and measured kitchens. The distance from cupboard to sink became something to investigate scientifically, not merely endure.

The institute brought together household teachers, chemists, nutrition researchers, sociologists, architects and engineers. Domestic work became a subject for specialist study. Recognizing its complexity challenged the idea that running a household required no expertise.

Modern housing projects promoted hot water, bathrooms and shared laundry rooms. The laundry was intended to reduce demanding domestic labour, especially women’s work. These were reform goals; the museum’s account does not prove identical facilities in every Swedish home.

Parental insurance introduced in 1974 allowed both mothers and fathers to take paid time away from employment to care for a newborn. The initial allowance was 180 days per child. Family care became a responsibility recognized through public policy.

In that first year, mothers took 99.5 percent of parental-benefit days. Giving both parents an entitlement did not immediately produce equal participation. The historical figures show a gap between a policy’s possibilities and everyday choices.

In October 1958, surgeon Åke Senning implanted a pacemaker developed by Rune Elmqvist in Arne Larsson. The museum preserves an early model from 1958 to 1960. This achievement concerned an implantable device; earlier external pacemakers already existed.

The first implanted device worked only for hours before replacement. Transistors helped make the equipment small enough, and later improvements increased reliability. A successful medical technology can emerge through repeated correction rather than a flawless first attempt.

Sweden entered the European Union on 1 January 1995, alongside Austria and Finland. Membership changed its international institutional relationships. It did not end Swedish statehood, language or local communities.

The constitution describes government through elected representatives and local self-government. It also identifies protection for cultural and linguistic minorities. These written principles reveal public commitments; assessing their implementation requires evidence beyond the wording of the law.

ending.text: Sweden continues as a state. Democratic reforms, the 1971 parliamentary reorganization and European membership in 1995 changed its institutions without representing national extinction. The atlas’s 1914 starting point is a coverage choice, not the kingdom’s founding date.
